title: AI Images, Video and Voices: Module Quiz

cards.prompt: Order the stages of an AI picture, from start to finish.

items.label: Random static, like a fuzzy TV

cards.explanation: Random static, blobs of colour, rough shapes, details, the finished picture.

cards.prompt: Why does the same image prompt give a different picture each time?

options.text: The model learns from each picture and changes it
Each picture starts from different random static
It reads the words in a different order each time
It uses a different model when the app is busy

cards.explanation: Each picture starts from **different random static**, so the steps lead somewhere different, while still matching the words.

cards.prompt: Possible clue that a picture is AI-made, or not a clue?

items.label: A shop sign with jumbled letters
A grainy photo from a concert
A blurry photo of a dog running

cards.explanation: Mismatched earrings and jumbled letters can be AI give-aways. Grainy and blurry photos are just normal photos.

cards.prompt: A viral picture has no watermark. Your friend says that proves it's real. Are they right?

options.text: Yes: AI tools always add a watermark you can see
Yes: a hidden watermark would show up when you share it
No: watermarks get cropped or stripped, and many tools add none
No: a picture with no watermark is always made by AI

cards.explanation: Watermarks get cropped, screenshots can strip hidden information saved with the file, and many tools add none. No watermark proves **nothing** either way.

cards.prompt: A video of your principal says school is closed tomorrow. It's spreading in a group chat started by someone you don't know.

steps.text: What's the best thing to do?

choices.text: Watch it again to check the lips match the words
choices.consequence: They match. Good fakes pass that test. Check with the real source instead.

choices.text: Check the school's website or ask a parent to call the school
choices.consequence: The school says it's open as normal. The video was a deepfake.
If it's fake, you're spreading it. Check first.

cards.explanation: An unknown sender and a surprising message are **situation clues**. Check with the real source, another way: the school's website or a call.

cards.prompt: Helpful or harmful use of face and voice AI?

items.label: An author's voice cloned, with their OK
A video translated with the speaker's OK
A fake call to get bank details
A fake video of a classmate as a prank

cards.explanation: With the person's **permission** and nobody fooled, it helps. Fakes that trick or embarrass people harm.

cards.prompt: Match each word to what it means.

pairs.right: Fake video of a real person
A mark saying AI made it

cards.explanation: **Generative AI** makes new things; a **deepfake** fakes a real person; a **voice clone** copies a voice; a **watermark** marks something as AI-made.
